title: Which Has More?
trouble: Children pick the group that looks bigger or longer, not the one with more.

blocks.html: Which group has more? You can count both groups, or match them up one by one. The group with some left over has more!

blocks.name: pk-pic
blocks.cap: Are there more apples or more bananas?

blocks.html: More means a bigger number. Match them up: the group with extras has more.

blocks.title: Apples and bananas
blocks.q: 5 apples and 3 bananas. Which has more?
steps: Match one apple to each banana.

blocks.html: For the grown-up: Compare at snack time: “Who has more grapes?” Line the things up side by side so your child can see the extras. Spread-out things can look like more, so lining up helps. Short and happy beats long. Five minutes is a good lesson.

items: Try it at home: Compare two piles of blocks.
Line up forks and spoons to see which has more.
Count cars of two colors on the street.
